causal_chain: Candidate-conditioned routing can select the most supportive capsule for a target item while a disagreement term suppresses capsules that actively conflict with that target.
If those errors are common in ML-1M full-sort evaluation, NDCG@10 should improve over a matched single-vector control.
Learning multiple user-specific intent capsules from the train-only interaction set allows different subsets of a user's history to specialize around distinct preference modes.
This selective support-minus-conflict scoring should reduce ranking errors where a held-out item is relevant to one user sub-interest but diluted by unrelated historical interactions.
Users with mixed tastes are poorly summarized by a single static collaborative vector.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameter count or stronger nonlinear scoring rather than from multi-intent capsule routing with explicit conflict suppression.
discriminative_predictions: A mechanism-off ablation that keeps parameter budget similar but collapses capsules into one pooled user vector should lose most of the gain if capsule specialization is the true cause.
If improvements are only due to extra capacity, then matched-width single-vector controls should recover most of the effect; if not, the frontier mechanism should retain a measurable gap.
Removing the conflict subtraction while retaining multi-capsule support should disproportionately hurt cases where user histories mix substitutes or unrelated tastes.
The proposed model should show its largest advantage for users with longer and more category-diverse training histories, while showing small or no gain for users with short homogeneous histories.
expected_evidence: Ablation comparison among full model, no-conflict variant, and single-pooled matched control.
Inspection of learned capsule assignment concentration showing different history items specializing to different capsules for mixed-interest users.
Per-user NDCG@10 stratified by history length and entropy-like item diversity.
Runtime and memory measurements confirming feasibility within candidate-local frozen-protocol limits.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched-capacity mechanism-off control with the same embeddings, optimizer family, and pairwise training matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, or if gains do not concentrate at all among mixed-interest users, the capsule-routing explanation is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This introduces a new core representation and interaction structure: users are not modeled as one embedding or graph-propagated state but as a small set of learned intent capsules with candidate-conditioned routing and explicit support-versus-conflict aggregation. That capability is not a parameter tweak of existing BPR_MF or LIGHTGCN descendants and requires custom history-to-capsule computation and scoring logic.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small set of learned intent capsules induced from the user's train-history item embeddings, then scores each candidate by supportive capsule agreement minus conflicting capsule agreement, will outperform a matched single-vector collaborative filter on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 because it can preserve minority sub-interests that static user embeddings average away.
implementation_requirements: For each candidate item, compute support score from the best-aligned capsule and conflict penalty from the most opposed capsule, then combine them into a scalar ranking score.
Implement a RecBole GeneralRecommender with train-history lookup tensors per user built only from the frozen training split.
Learn global item embeddings plus a capsule initialization matrix and routing network that maps a user's interacted item embeddings into K user intent capsules.
Provide executable ablations for mechanism-off and no-conflict variants within the same candidate-local codebase.
Support full-sort inference over all items for evaluation.
Train with pairwise BPR-style loss under the frozen protocol using sampled negatives from training only.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same item embedding dimensionality, optimizer family, pairwise loss family, training data, and comparable parameter budget, but replace capsule routing with a single pooled user representation and remove conflict subtraction.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace single-vector user scoring with a multi-capsule user representation computed from historical item embeddings, plus candidate-conditioned support selection and explicit conflict subtraction in the score.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off control: keep the same item embeddings and pairwise training pipeline, but summarize each user's history into one attention-pooled vector, score by its dot product with the candidate item, and remove both multi-capsule routing and conflict subtraction.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Implement K-user-intent capsules derived from train-history item embeddings and compare against a matched single-pooled-history control, with the smallest novel component being candidate-conditioned capsule selection plus one opposing-capsule penalty term.
blind_projection.research_question: Does explicit user multi-intent capsule routing with conflict-aware scoring provide ranking signal beyond what matched single-vector collaborative filters can express under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with small capsule count (for example 3-4), padded user train histories, and simple routing iterations should fit the development budget because ML-1M is modest in scale and the model can avoid graph propagation and expensive sequence encoders.
